_comment: Modeled on christybmanjila/healthcare-assurance-demo's test-data/healthcare.json: flat key -> {value, _note?} fixtures for kane-cli scenarios to reference by name instead of hard-coding values in prose. Built by reading website/server.py directly (the actual app state), not requirements/book-publishing-website.md — that doc currently describes a different app shape (price-per-book, SKU tiles, cart, purchase/edition flow) than server.py implements (a self-publishing platform: browse a read-only book showcase with no price/checkout, submit a manuscript into a package seat, track/withdraw submissions). Reconcile the requirements doc against server.py before running `kane-cli design tests` against it, or generated scenarios will assert behavior (cart, SKU, purchase) the app doesn't have.

search_term_title_match._note: Matches exactly one book by title substring: 'The Willow Hour'. Verified against the live BOOKS catalog (case-insensitive substring match on title/author/genre).

search_term_genre_match._note: Matches all 20 Fantasy books via the genre field — use when a test needs multiple results rather than exactly one.

genre_total_count._note: Every genre is padded to CATALOG_SIZE_PER_GENRE=20 in server.py's _extend_catalog(), so this count is the same for all 6 genres, not just Fantasy.

genre_first_title_sort_by_title._note: Fantasy books sorted by title (server's default sort=title) — resolved from the live catalog, not guessed; will break if BOOKS or the wordbank-generated titles change.

genre_first_title_sort_by_rating._note: Fantasy books sorted by rating desc (rating 4.9, the highest in the genre).

book_package_name._note: This book was published via the authors-choice package — book_detail.html links to /publish/authors-choice as 'Published via our Author's Choice package.'

home_book_count._note: len(BOOKS) after catalog extension — shown on the home page as '120+ books published through our platform'.

featured_book_title._note: Top of the home page's 4 featured books (sorted by rating desc, rating 4.9 is the catalog max). No tie at rank 1, so this is stable; ranks 2-4 tie at 4.8 and their order depends on BOOKS list order — don't assert on those without re-checking.

scarce_package_id._note: Only 1 seat ('Seat 1') exists for this package all month — the one package where 'fully booked this month' is reachable by claiming a single seat, analogous to how the healthcare demo picks a doctor/slot with exactly one remaining opening.

scarce_package_preseed_url._note: Hit this with a throwaway HTTP client (curl, not the browser under test) BEFORE the suite starts, the same way healthcare's preseed_bookings() claims a slot server-side with zero agent-interpretation risk. taken_seats is process-global in server.py, so claiming this seat from any session makes /publish/authors-choice show 'Fully booked this month' and package_full's error text for every subsequent session, including the one under test. Don't navigate the test browser itself to this URL — that would also add a submission row to ITS OWN session, contaminating My Submissions assertions.

genres_list.value: Biography, Fantasy, Fiction, Mystery, Non-Fiction, Sci-Fi

new_manuscript_package_id._note: Standard has 4 seats — large enough that a normal submit-flow test won't starve the scarce_package_id fixture above (which needs authors-choice's single seat left untouched).

author_with_existing_submission.value: a fresh browser session where you first navigate to http://localhost:5050/dev/seed?submit=standard:Seat%202:New%20Manuscript:The%20Salt%20Almanac:Priya%20Osei:priya.osei@example.com:Non-Fiction&next=/my-submissions before proceeding to Step 1; this pre-seeds exactly one submission into THIS session (via the app's own test-fixture route, not by asking you to fill out the form) and lands you on My Submissions.
author_with_existing_submission._note: Session-scoped fixture, so unlike scarce_package_preseed_url this one IS meant to be visited by the test browser itself — submissions live in the Flask session cookie, same reason healthcare's patient_with_booked_appointments couldn't be preseeded server-side. Using /dev/seed instead of prose ('book an appointment first') removes the agent-interpretation risk healthcare's README flagged for that pattern.

author_with_cancelable_submission.value: a fresh browser session where you first navigate to http://localhost:5050/dev/seed?submit=standard:Seat%203:Revised%20Manuscript:The%20Long%20Gate:Marlowe%20Finch:marlowe.finch@example.com:Biography&next=/my-submissions before proceeding to Step 1; this is the submission that is safe to withdraw.

submission_reference_example._note: Format only, from contact.html's example text — actual IDs are assigned sequentially starting at SUB-1001 per process lifetime, so don't assert an exact number without seeding submission order deterministically first.
